Yeah, I'm not wildly convinced that stealing guys is a huge issue. I
mean, yeah, it blows a lot of the time, but many things do. The ones
that steal guys most often are all kind of self correcting (other than
"block the action" or "DI them"):

-Temptation: If you are stealing someone with Temptation and getting
that much blood off of them with Heidleburg, it took them, what, 11
turns to save up enough counters? That is plenty of time to either take
the blood off, use it, or win the game.

-Mind Rape: This is the brutal one, but at least you have a turn to do
something about all the blood you are about to lose (Minion Tap or burn
the Heidleburg or spend the blood or something). With Enkil Cog, it is
kind of a particularly brutal combo, but then you need to have Enkil Cog
*and* Heidleburg *and* Mind Rape *and* stealth to get the action through
all the same time. I suspect that this particular horror show will fail
to work far more often than it won't.

-Spirit Marionette: If there is someone on the table with OBE and
Heidleburg, be sure to keep all you big guys tapped.



Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:
On Jan 12, 1:51 pm, Jeff Kuta <jeff.k...@gmail.com> wrote:

> On Jan 12, 1:05 pm, XZealot <xzea...@cox.net> wrote:
>
> > Should Heidleburg be banned?
>

> No. Ban Temptation, Mind Rape and Spirit Marionette.
>
> Heidelberg isn't the problem. Minion stealing is.
>

> Jeff

Minion stealing is not balanced. It unduly punishes large vampires
like everything that messes "equally" with minions punishes large
vampires. It can be incredibly unfun to play against a minion steal
deck.

However, at what point does trying to fix problems become burning the
house down and starting over?

I do have a problem with Heidelberg's ability to end players' games so
easily in minion steal decks. It's simply not as easy as people seem
to think to stop someone from Spirit Marionetteing or Temptationing or
whatever your minions away, really the best answer is to get the steal
deck ousted as quickly as possible since it isn't likely to be awesome
on pool defense. Metagamewise, the decks are held in check by how
they often aren't nearly as efficient at ousting as less complicated
plans and how stealing vampires from weenie decks isn't likely to stop
the weenies from killing you.

But, I have trouble elevating Heidelberg to the top of the list of
"wished were different".
